issues.description: raise PerformanceWarning conflates a warning class with a hard exception, breaking the warn-vs-error contract.
issues.detail: PerformanceWarning is a Warning subclass meant for warnings.warn(), not raise. The test pins this with pytest.raises(PerformanceWarning), institutionalizing the confusion. Decide the contract: either warnings.warn() and let the caller proceed, or raise a proper Error subclass (ValueError/RuntimeError). The docstring, message text, and code currently tell three different stories.

issues.description: Unreachable `break` after `raise` is dead code signalling unresolved loop semantics.
issues.detail: `raise` exits the frame, so the following `break` can never execute. The dead statement reveals the author was unsure whether to fail-fast on the first misaligned axis or aggregate all offenders. Pick one postcondition — first-failure or report-all — document it, and delete the other branch.

issues.description: safe_chunk_size computation is dimensionally suspect and leaks internals as user-facing advice.
issues.detail: `np.prod(zarr_write_chunks) * max(1, z.dtype.itemsize)` collapses a per-axis tuple into a scalar and presents it as a recommended `array.chunk-size` value, but the mapping between that config and resulting per-axis chunks is not linear. The `max(1, itemsize)` guard is dead — numpy itemsize is always >=1 for real dtypes. State the precondition you are advising; don't fabricate a number.

issues.description: `not nominal_dask_chunk_size % zw == 0` relies on operator precedence; rewrite as `!= 0`.
issues.detail: Python parses this correctly only by accident of precedence. A reader must simulate the parser to verify intent. Replace with `nominal_dask_chunk_size % zw != 0` — one operator, obvious intent. Guard clauses should not require precedence recall.

issues.description: Validation policy belongs in an extracted helper, not inline in to_zarr.
issues.detail: The 20-line block computing dask_write_chunks, iterating axes, formatting messages, and deciding raise/warn mixes write-mechanism with config-resolution policy. Extract a pure `validate_shard_alignment(zarr_chunks, dask_chunks, dtype) -> Optional[str]` (or `_resolve_write_chunks`) so to_zarr decides what to do with the result. Data in, message out, no embedded policy.

issues.description: Region path may bypass or violate the alignment invariant after new_blockdim.
issues.detail: The misalignment check runs before the `if region is None` branch, but the region path constructs chunks via `new_blockdim(s, c, r)` which may produce chunks violating the just-verified invariant. State and verify the postcondition that all chunks passed to rechunk remain multiples of zarr_write_chunks along every axis, including after new_blockdim.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the diff's core idea — using shard shape as previous_chunks to drive auto-aligned dask chunks — is sound, but the new validation block has two blocking defects. First, `raise PerformanceWarning(...)` conflates a warning class with a hard exception, and the test enshrines this confusion via pytest.raises; the contract (warn vs. error) must be picked explicitly. Second, the unreachable `break` after `raise` is dead code that reveals undecided loop semantics (fail-fast vs. report-all). Secondary cleanups: rewrite the precedence-fragile `not x % y == 0` guard, fix the dimensionally suspect safe_chunk_size advice, extract the alignment policy into a pure helper, and verify the region path still satisfies the invariant.
